sections.heading: C2 — Traffic signals
sections.markdown:
## C2 — Traffic signals

FACT_ID: sec03-R01 | anchor: A02
An overhead green arrow pointing downward means its lane may be used. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-R02 | anchor: A02
An overhead steady yellow X warns that the lane's travel direction will reverse, so prepare to leave that lane safely. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-R03 | anchor: A02
An overhead steady red X prohibits using the lane beneath it. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-R04 | anchor: A02
A steady white one-way left-turn arrow over a lane restricts traffic in that lane to left turns. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-R05 | anchor: A02
A steady white two-way left-turn arrow marks a lane used only for left turns and shared with opposing left-turning traffic. [A02]
Source: [A02 -> pdf-0012]

FACT_ID: sec03-R06 | anchor: A03
Pedestrians must follow WALK and DON'T WALK indications or their walking-person and raised-hand symbols. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R07 | anchor: A03
Where an intersection lacks pedestrian signals, pedestrians must obey its red, yellow and green traffic lights. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R08 | anchor: A03
Drivers must stay alert for pedestrians who disregard signals and must still yield to them. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R09 | anchor: A03
A steady WALK indication allows a pedestrian to begin crossing while watching for turning vehicles that may fail to yield. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R10 | anchor: A03
When DON'T WALK or the raised hand starts flashing, a pedestrian already in the street should finish crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R11 | anchor: A03
When DON'T WALK or the raised hand starts flashing, a pedestrian still at the curb must not begin crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R12 | anchor: A03
A steady DON'T WALK indication or steady raised hand prohibits crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R13 | anchor: A03
Near a blind pedestrian using a white cane or guide dog, slow down, yield, proceed cautiously and be ready to stop to prevent harm. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R14 | anchor: A03
When school-zone yellow lights flash or the sign's stated time applies, the maximum permitted speed is 15 mph. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R15 | anchor: A03
Speeding in a school zone adds three points to the driving record and also leads to a fine. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R16 | anchor: A03
Approach railroad crossings cautiously, looking both ways and listening for trains or warning signals before crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R17 | anchor: A03
A railroad crossing requires a stop when flashing red lights, a lowered gate, a flagger or an audible train warning indicates an approaching train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R18 | anchor: A03
Do not bypass a railroad gate or disregard a signal announcing an approaching train. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R19 | anchor: A03
At a railroad crossing without signals, reduce speed and prepare to stop if an approaching train is seen or heard. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R20 | anchor: A03
Cross railroad tracks cautiously only after all warning signals have ended and there is evidence that no train is approaching. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R21 | anchor: A03
At a railroad crossing, you should stop if an approaching train has sounded an audible warning, or if an approaching train is plainly visible and dangerously close to the crossing. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R22 | anchor: A03
Never stop a vehicle on railroad tracks, even when no train seems to be coming. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]

FACT_ID: sec03-R23 | anchor: A03
When traffic backs up near a railroad crossing, stop where the entire vehicle remains clear of the rails. [A03]
Source: [A03 -> pdf-0013]
